snippet.title: "The Brothers Concerto" by Leonardo and Peter Dugan Teaser
snippet.description:
The Brothers Concerto revisits life moments that encapsulate the unique experience of siblinghood: Tales of make-believe monsters. An anxious car ride. A little brother glad to tag along with his big brother, unknowingly developing the foundation of their closeness and mutual respect in adulthood. Unfaltering support through life’s greatest challenges.

Leonardo and Peter Dugan grew up in Philadelphia, where their musical development was steeped in both the jazz and classical traditions. The language of the Concerto reflects the commonality and individuality of brothers, of two musical idioms, of an orchestra and its soloist. Soaring, lyrical melodies, propulsive rhythms, and Leonardo’s characteristic lush orchestration frame the athletic virtuosity of Peter’s pianism. It’s an inspired combination—classical structure and counterpoint with improvised solos using the vocabulary of jazz.

snippet.title: The Cliburn Agency
snippet.description:
The Cliburn Agency is a full-service boutique firm that offers comprehensive general management, concert booking, project management, and publicity and branding services to a select group of rising and established instrumentalists—piano and beyond—whose high artistic caliber is matched by a vision for moving the field of classical music forward.

The Cliburn Agency roster comprises Anderson & Roe Piano Duo (@andersonroe);  Greg Anderson, piano (@gregandersonpiano) ; Peter Dugan, piano (@peterdugan9983) ; Fei-Fei, piano (@feifeipianist) ; Bridget Kibbey, harp (@bridgetkibbey);  Joshua Roman, cello (@JoshuaRomanCello) ; and Clayton Stephenson, piano (@Claytonplayspiano) . From intriguing programming and projects to alternative concerts and community engagement, the touring musicians of the Agency roster are dedicated to connection and creativity—and they are partnering with the Cliburn to enhance and magnify their careers, efforts, and impact.

Learn more at https://cliburnagency.com/

“The Cliburn Agency is a compelling expansion of the Cliburn’s brand and impact. Our core mission is to support artists and continuously advance classical music. The management and promotion of exceptional musicians—particularly those with a specific fervor and dedication for expanding audiences and breaking down barriers—is the next step in realizing that mission. Through this new program, the Cliburn develops another powerful way to meet the moment and find new ways to expand classical music’s reach as a source of commonality and shared experience in today’s world.”
– Jacques Marquis, president & CEO

snippet.title: Vitaly Starikov: Cliburn 2025 SCHUMANN Symphonic Etudes, op. 13
snippet.description:
Seventeenth Van Cliburn International Piano Competition
Quarterfinal Round Recital
May 25, 2025
Van Cliburn Concert Hall at TCU

Vitaly Starikov - SILVER MEDALIST
Israel/Russia
Age 30

SCHUMANN Symphonic Etudes, op. 13

About Vitaly

Russian/Israeli pianist Vitaly Starikov has found distinction with “raw, deeply felt, and powerful” (La Scena) performances, while having an unassuming onstage presence and a “willingness less to play at the audience than to draw [them] into musical intimacies” (Dallas Morning News). His bold approach won him silver at the 2025 Van Cliburn International Piano Competition and the admiration of fans around the globe. Vitaly’s perspective on music is manifested in his repertoire: he presents music that reflects not only tradition, but also contemporary life, striving to offer new perspectives on familiar music and introduce lesser-known pieces to wider audiences. His Cliburn performance of Bartok’s Second Piano Concerto electrified the room, with a La Scena reviewer noting that “he understood this music, and gave an impactful, lively, and gripping interpretation on all levels: emotionally, architecturally, and in terms of his sound palette.”

Recital and chamber music appearances have taken him around the world, notably to Austria, Australia, Slovakia, Israel, Cyprus, Italy, France, Belgium, and Malaysia, with highlights including Sydney Opera House, Queen Elisabeth Hall, and the Great Hall of the Moscow Conservatory. He has performed with the Antwerp and Belgian National Orchestras, Sydney Symphony Orchestra, Belarusian State Symphony Orchestra, and St. Petersburg Symphony, and toured with the Orchestre national de Metz Grand Est. This inaugural Cliburn season takes him to the Bravo! Vail and Sunriver Music Festivals; Colorado Springs Philharmonic, and Pacific, Topeka, and Springfield Symphony Orchestras, and in recitals throughout the United States.

Born into a family of musicians, Vitaly’s journey started when his parents enrolled him to sing in a children’s music group at age 3, and he went on to Ural Musical School for Gifted Children in his native Yekaterinburg at 7. He made his concerto debut at age 10 with the Ural State Russian Folk Orchestra, and his recital debut three years later, in the small hall of the Ural Special Music School. It was at 14 that he committed his life to music. His “dream came true” when he began studying with Vera Gornostayeva, one of the world’s most venerated teachers, at the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory. He went on to earn his bachelor’s degree at the Conservatory and then his master’s degree, under the tutelage of Eliso Virsaladze. He’s now at the Yale School of Music, pursuing an artist diploma under Boris Berman.

snippet.title: Aristo Sham: 2025 Cliburn RACHMANINOV Études-tableaux, op. 39
snippet.description:
Seventeenth Van Cliburn International Piano Competition
Semifinal Round Recital
May 28, 2025
Bass Performance Hall

Aristo Sham - GOLD MEDALIST
Hong Kong, China
Age 29

RACHMANINOV Études-tableaux, op. 39

ABOUT ARISTO
Pianist Aristo Sham exudes astounding intellect and a deep emotional resonance; a cultivated sophistication and an immediately engaging presence; a penchant to take on the great monuments of the piano repertoire and a natural, infectious spontaneity. This makeup is fueled by a fascination with the world and its rich cultures: he was an international prodigy, is a voracious student of wide-ranging interests, and currently splits his time between three continents.  

At the 2025 Van Cliburn International Piano Competition, Aristo found his breakthrough moment, taking home both the gold medal and the audience award at “one of the most prestigious contests in classical music” (The New York Times, June 2022). And the critics showered him with imaginative praise, calling him “a marvel of deft characterization,” “consistently authoritative,” “a card-carrying risk taker,” “a dapper, aristocratic ﬁgure on stage,” “a pianist I look forward to hearing again” (The Dallas Morning News, Gramophone, Texas Classical Voice). In just two months’ time, he was mentioned in more than 800 news articles, and his Cliburn performance videos were streamed 2 million times across 125 countries.  

Aristo was featured in the 2009 documentary The World’s Greatest Musical Prodigies on Channel 4 (UK), has performed for royalty including King Charles, and was hailed by The New York Times in 2020 as an artist “whose playing combines clarity, elegance and abundant technique.” He has concertized across Asia, Europe, and the United States, with major highlights including the London Symphony Orchestra under Sir Simon Rattle, Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra under Edo de Waart, English Chamber Orchestra under the late Sir Raymond Leppard, Orchestre de Chambre de Lausanne, and Minnesota Orchestra. His 2025–2026 debut season as Cliburn winner includes a major tour of Asia through South Korea and China, and U.S. recitals for Aspen Music Festival, La Jolla Music Society/The Conrad, UCSB Arts and Lectures, and the Skyline Piano Artist Series at Northwestern University. 

Recently, he recorded and hosted the complete Brahms solo piano music on RTHK4, Classical Radio in Hong Kong. Upcoming seasons will see the release of two albums on Platoon: a Cliburn live release, as well as his debut studio album.  

Aristo Sham’s mother taught piano in their Hong Kong home, so he says: “I was enveloped in the environment of the piano even before I was born.” His parents recall his immense curiosity towards the instrument when he was a toddler and started him in lessons when he was 3. At the age of 10, he began competing and concertizing. But he also went to regular schools, never making the conscious decision to focus solely on the piano or his other studies; this made the dual degree program at Harvard and the New England Conservatory a perfect ﬁt when he went to college. He ﬁnished his Bachelor of Arts at Harvard in 2019 and master’s at NEC under Victor Rosenbaum in 2020. He then went to the Ingesund School of Music in Sweden to study with Julia Mustonen-Dahlkvist before returning to the States to earn an artist diploma at The Juilliard School with Robert McDonald and Orli Shaham. In addition to the Cliburn, he’s a laureate of international competitions, with ﬁrst-prize wins at Young Concert Artists, Ettlingen, Gina Bachauer, and Monte Carlo Music Masters.

snippet.description:
Cliburn Backstage with Greg Anderson (‪@gregandersonpiano)
Interviews, curation, and editing by Greg Anderson

Seventeenth Van Cliburn International Piano Competition
May 21–June 7, 2025

Watch Carter's Ravel Piano Concerto for the Left Hand: https://youtu.be/gwaEeOTXhuQ

Carter Johnson, Canada/United States, 28
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/carter-johnson

About Carter
Carter Johnson only ever remembers wanting to become a concert pianist since his grandmother encouraged him toward the instrument when he was 5. Growing up on Vancouver Island, he studied with Shelley Roberts for 12 years before attending the University of British Columbia, where he completed a bachelor’s under Mark Anderson. He moved to the United States in 2019 to study with Joseph Kalichstein and Matti Raekallio at The Juilliard School (master’s) and has spent the last four years in New Haven, living with his wife and two children while attending the Yale School of Music under the tutelage of Wei-Yi Yang (master’s and now doctorate studies).  

The silver medalist of the 2024 Gina Bachauer International Piano Competition, he has performed with the Montréal Symphony Orchestra, Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra, Orchestre Métropolitain, Utah Symphony, Poznań Philharmonic Orchestra, Victoria Symphony Orchestra, and Orchestra of the Americas, and his playing has been broadcasted by CBC Radio and medici.tv. Venue highlights include the Maison Symphonique, Chan Centre for the Performing Arts, Kaufmann Concert Hall at the 92nd Street Y, Shenzhen Concert Hall, Salle Bourgie, and Warsaw National Philharmonic Hall. 

Carter has a particular interest in bringing light to lesser-explored parts of the repertory, most recently championing a collection of works by nearly forgotten Polish composers. He’s an experienced vocal coach, is enthusiastic about languages, and has also studied oboe, voice, and harpsichord. Trained in elocution as a teenager, he holds an ATCL with distinction in speech and drama from Trinity College London, which serves him well in recital: he loves speaking with audiences to bring them further into the music and its story. He also finds great inspiration outside of classical music—in his family, film, nature, food, and non-classical artists like Björk and Brian Eno, whom he says help him to think outside the box.

Angel Stanislav Wang, United States, 22
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/angel-stanislav-wang

About Angel
Angel Stanislav Wang was born into a family of musicians in Los Angeles. His pianist parents are U.S. immigrants—his father originally from China, his mother from Russia—who established a music school in their longtime home in California. Angel was always extremely fond of performing on stage, whether playing the piano, dancing, or singing. As a small child, he would put on shows in their living room, paying careful attention to each detail, from lighting and special effects to costumes and sets. “Classical music was always present. When I first heard the works of Rachmaninov and Tchaikovsky, I ran to the piano, trying to repeat the beautiful harmonic shifts and endless melodies that captivated me when listening to these composers.” His mother began serious piano lessons with him when he was 5, and he immediately showed immense promise. Wanting him to be trained in the same school of music that she had, his mother moved him to her native Moscow in 2013, where he would live with his grandparents and attend the Gnessin Special School of Music (with Tatiana Zelikman). He joined Natalia Trull’s studio at Central Music School and then the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory in 2020, where he continues to study today. 

A winner of more than 35 international competitions (and a silver medal at the 2023 Tchaikovsky), Angel regularly concertizes in the United States, Germany, Russia, Switzerland, Austria, Spain, Italy, Croatia; he’s performed at Carnegie Hall, Musikverein (Vienna, Austria), the Great, Small, and Rachmaninov Halls of the Moscow Conservatory, Concert Halls of the Mariinsky Theatre (St. Petersburg), and Tchaikovsky Concert Hall (Moscow). The 22-year-old loves traveling to different countries: “Whenever I have the chance, I visit different museums, theatres, and art exhibitions. It is interesting to experience the different cultures, mentalities, and ideas, as well as interests, of other people.”

Philipp Lynov, Russia, 26
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/philipp-lynov

About Philipp
Philipp Lynov saw a piano for the first time when he was in kindergarten. The moment left such a lasting impression on him that he credits it—the fascination of owning a piano and childhood curiosity—with his start in music. He started learning at the age of 6 as “simply a source of joy,” then earned a spot at the Central Music School at the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory at the age of 14, studying with Natalia Bogdanova. He went on to complete his bachelor’s there as well, under Eliso Virsaladze. He then moved to Germany, where he's studied with Claudio Martinez Mehner and Nina Tichman at the Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln since 2022.  

Philipp has won first prizes at international competitions, including Xiamen (China), Takamatsu (Japan), and Paderewski (Poland), among others. Concerts have taken him around the globe—to Russia, Germany, Austria, Poland, Spain, Italy, Israel, Switzerland, Australia, and Japan—with highlights including his 2023 debut in the Main Auditorium of the Berlin Philharmonic with the Sinfonieorchester Berlin. When it comes to engaging audiences, he says: “I believe that every person possesses their own unique brilliance. To captivate audiences with music, it’s essential to communicate something meaningful—something that, while not always easy to define, resonates deeply.”

Evren Ozel, United States, 36
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/evren-ozel

About Evren
Evren Ozel’s start in piano was very simple: at the age of 3, he was asked if he wanted to take lessons, and he said yes. Right away, these lessons were his favorite part of the week. “If I got in trouble with my mom, the threat that would set me straight was the threat of taking me out of piano lessons.” After his first international piano competition when he was 14, he was inspired to pursue music professionally. “The colleagues I met who shared an interest in playing music, and the immense repertoire that I learned about over those two weeks helped me understand what an incredibly deep and enriching world that pianists live in.” He’s attended the New England Conservatory of Music in Boston since 2017, studying with Wha Kyung Byun and earning his bachelor’s, master’s, and artist diploma; he is now part of the NEC Institute for Concert Artists. 

Evren is the recipient of 2023 Avery Fisher and 2022 Salon de Virtuosi Career Grants, and a laureate of the Cleveland, Dublin, and Cooper International Piano Competitions. He has been represented by Concert Artists Guild since 2021 as a winner of their Victor Elmaleh Competition. Since his debut with the Minnesota Orchestra at age 11, he has been a featured soloist with the Cleveland Orchestra, Jacksonville Symphony, and Boston Pops Orchestra. He’s performed recitals at La Jolla Music Society, Capital Region Classical, Cal Performances, Schubert Club, Chopin Society of Minnesota, and The Gilmore. His first album of Mozart Concertos with the ORF Radio Symphony of Vienna and conductor Howard Griffiths will be released this year on Alpha Classics. An active chamber musician, he performs alongside artists including Stella Chen, Zlatomir Fung, Paul Huang, and Kim Kashkashian. He spent four summers at the Marlboro Festival and is currently a 2024–2027 Bowers Program Artist for the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center.

About Evren
Evren Ozel’s start in piano was very simple: at the age of 3, he was asked if he wanted to take lessons, and he said yes. Right away, these lessons were his favorite part of the week. “If I got in trouble with my mom, the threat that would set me straight was the threat of taking me out of piano lessons.” After his first international piano competition when he was 14, he was inspired to pursue music professionally. “The colleagues I met who shared an interest in playing music, and the immense repertoire that I learned about over those two weeks helped me understand what an incredibly deep and enriching world that pianists live in.” He’s attended the New England Conservatory of Music in Boston since 2017, studying with Wha Kyung Byun and earning his bachelor’s, master’s, and artist diploma; he is now part of the NEC Institute for Concert Artists. 

Evren is the recipient of 2023 Avery Fisher and 2022 Salon de Virtuosi Career Grants, and a laureate of the Cleveland, Dublin, and Cooper International Piano Competitions. He has been represented by Concert Artists Guild since 2021 as a winner of their Victor Elmaleh Competition. Since his debut with the Minnesota Orchestra at age 11, he has been a featured soloist with the Cleveland Orchestra, Jacksonville Symphony, and Boston Pops Orchestra. He’s performed recitals at La Jolla Music Society, Capital Region Classical, Cal Performances, Schubert Club, Chopin Society of Minnesota, and The Gilmore. His first album of Mozart Concertos with the ORF Radio Symphony of Vienna and conductor Howard Griffiths will be released this year on Alpha Classics. An active chamber musician, he performs alongside artists including Stella Chen, Zlatomir Fung, Paul Huang, and Kim Kashkashian. He spent four summers at the Marlboro Festival and is currently a 2024–2027 Bowers Program Artist for the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center.

About Philipp
Philipp Lynov saw a piano for the first time when he was in kindergarten. The moment left such a lasting impression on him that he credits it—the fascination of owning a piano and childhood curiosity—with his start in music. He started learning at the age of 6 as “simply a source of joy,” then earned a spot at the Central Music School at the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory at the age of 14, studying with Natalia Bogdanova. He went on to complete his bachelor’s there as well, under Eliso Virsaladze. He then moved to Germany, where he's studied with Claudio Martinez Mehner and Nina Tichman at the Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln since 2022.  

Philipp has won first prizes at international competitions, including Xiamen (China), Takamatsu (Japan), and Paderewski (Poland), among others. Concerts have taken him around the globe—to Russia, Germany, Austria, Poland, Spain, Italy, Israel, Switzerland, Australia, and Japan—with highlights including his 2023 debut in the Main Auditorium of the Berlin Philharmonic with the Sinfonieorchester Berlin. When it comes to engaging audiences, he says: “I believe that every person possesses their own unique brilliance. To captivate audiences with music, it’s essential to communicate something meaningful—something that, while not always easy to define, resonates deeply.”

SCHUMANN Piano Concerto in A Minor, op. 54

About Vitaly
Born into a family of musicians, Vitaly Starikov’s journey started when his parents enrolled him to sing in a children’s music group at age 3, and he went on to Ural Musical School for Gifted Children in his native Yekaterinburg at 7. He made his concerto debut at age 10 with the Ural State Russian Folk Orchestra, and his recital debut three years later, in the small hall of the Ural Special Music School. It was at 14 that he committed his life to music. His “dream came true” when he began studying with Vera Gornostayeva, one of the world’s most venerated teachers, at the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory. At that time, her student, Vadym Kholodenko, had just won the 2013 Cliburn Competition, which greatly inspired Vitaly: “and it was then that the thought was born to someday participate in this competition.” He went on to earn his bachelor’s degree at the Conservatory and then his master’s degree, under the tutelage of Eliso Virsaladze. He’s now at the Yale School of Music, pursuing an artist diploma under Boris Berman and is a laureate of the Queen Elisabeth and Sydney International Competitions.

Recital and chamber music appearances have taken him around the world, notably to Austria, Australia, Slovakia, Israel, Cyprus, Italy, France, Belgium, and Malaysia, with highlights including Sydney Opera House, Queen Elisabeth Hall, and the Great Hall of the Moscow Conservatory. He has performed with the Antwerp and Belgian National Orchestras, Sydney Symphony Orchestra, Belarusian State Symphony Orchestra, and St. Petersburg Symphony, and toured with the Orchestre national de Metz Grand Est. He holds a strong commitment to new music and has won accolades for his performances of it, including at the Queen Elisabeth (Belgium), Jaen (Spain), and Taneyev (Russia) international competitions. “I want to present works that reflect not only tradition but also contemporary life, offering new perspectives on familiar music and introducing lesser-known pieces to wider audiences.”

RAVEL Piano Concerto for the Left Hand in D Major

About Carter
Carter Johnson only ever remembers wanting to become a concert pianist since his grandmother encouraged him toward the instrument when he was 5. Growing up on Vancouver Island, he studied with Shelley Roberts for 12 years before attending the University of British Columbia, where he completed a bachelor’s under Mark Anderson. He moved to the United States in 2019 to study with Joseph Kalichstein and Matti Raekallio at The Juilliard School (master’s) and has spent the last four years in New Haven, living with his wife and two children while attending the Yale School of Music under the tutelage of Wei-Yi Yang (master’s and now doctorate studies).  

The silver medalist of the 2024 Gina Bachauer International Piano Competition, he has performed with the Montréal Symphony Orchestra, Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra, Orchestre Métropolitain, Utah Symphony, Poznań Philharmonic Orchestra, Victoria Symphony Orchestra, and Orchestra of the Americas, and his playing has been broadcasted by CBC Radio and medici.tv. Venue highlights include the Maison Symphonique, Chan Centre for the Performing Arts, Kaufmann Concert Hall at the 92nd Street Y, Shenzhen Concert Hall, Salle Bourgie, and Warsaw National Philharmonic Hall. 

Carter has a particular interest in bringing light to lesser-explored parts of the repertory, most recently championing a collection of works by nearly forgotten Polish composers. He’s an experienced vocal coach, is enthusiastic about languages, and has also studied oboe, voice, and harpsichord. Trained in elocution as a teenager, he holds an ATCL with distinction in speech and drama from Trinity College London, which serves him well in recital: he loves speaking with audiences to bring them further into the music and its story. He also finds great inspiration outside of classical music—in his family, film, nature, food, and non-classical artists like Björk and Brian Eno, whom he says help him to think outside the box.

Age 22

Marin Alsop, conductor

RACHMANINOV Piano Concerto No. 3 in D Minor, op. 30


About Angel
Angel Stanislav Wang was born into a family of musicians in Los Angeles. His pianist parents are U.S. immigrants—his father originally from China, his mother from Russia—who established a music school in their longtime home in California. Angel was always extremely fond of performing on stage, whether playing the piano, dancing, or singing. As a small child, he would put on shows in their living room, paying careful attention to each detail, from lighting and special effects to costumes and sets. “Classical music was always present. When I first heard the works of Rachmaninov and Tchaikovsky, I ran to the piano, trying to repeat the beautiful harmonic shifts and endless melodies that captivated me when listening to these composers.” His mother began serious piano lessons with him when he was 5, and he immediately showed immense promise. Wanting him to be trained in the same school of music that she had, his mother moved him to her native Moscow in 2013, where he would live with his grandparents and attend the Gnessin Special School of Music (with Tatiana Zelikman). He joined Natalia Trull’s studio at Central Music School and then the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory in 2020, where he continues to study today. 

A winner of more than 35 international competitions (and a silver medal at the 2023 Tchaikovsky), Angel regularly concertizes in the United States, Germany, Russia, Switzerland, Austria, Spain, Italy, Croatia; he’s performed at Carnegie Hall, Musikverein (Vienna, Austria), the Great, Small, and Rachmaninov Halls of the Moscow Conservatory, Concert Halls of the Mariinsky Theatre (St. Petersburg), and Tchaikovsky Concert Hall (Moscow). The 22-year-old loves traveling to different countries: “Whenever I have the chance, I visit different museums, theatres, and art exhibitions. It is interesting to experience the different cultures, mentalities, and ideas, as well as interests, of other people.”

snippet.title: 2025 Cliburn Backstage: Jonathan Mamora, Preliminary Round
snippet.description:
Cliburn Backstage with Greg Anderson (‪  ‪  @gregandersonpiano   )
Interviews, curation, and editing by Greg Anderson

Seventeenth Van Cliburn International Piano Competition
May 21–June 7, 2025

Jonathan Mamora, United States, 30
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/jonathan-mamora

About Jonathan
Jonathan Mamora remembers being a 4-year-old who was very jealous of his brother’s piano lessons. His father wanted them both to learn so that they could play in church, but the older sibling was enrolled first. Jonathan would listen, remember the notes his brother practiced, and then try to replicate them—eventually discovering on his own how the dots on the pages corresponded to the notes the instrument played. He says he was immediately hooked and has been ever since. 

The Indonesian-American, Southern California native earned a bachelor’s in music from La Sierra University with Elvin Rodriguez and a master’s at The Juilliard School with Hung-Kuan Chen. This year, he completed a doctorate from the Eastman School of Music under Douglas Humpherys. 
Jonathan is the first-prize winner of a number of international piano competitions, most recently the 2025 Hilton Head, 2023 Scottish, 2023 Maria Canals Barcelona, and 2022 Olga Kern. He has performed throughout North and South America, Europe, and Asia, with highlights including a 2023 debut at Carnegie Hall and engagements with the Royal Scottish National Orchestra, New Amsterdam Symphony Orchestra, and New Mexico Philharmonic. His career to date has been truly multifaceted: he’s been a church musician much of his life; enjoys collaborating with vocalists, instrumentalists, ensembles, and choirs; and has also performed as a percussionist, vocalist, historical keyboardist (harpsichord, fortepiano), and conductor. 

Jonathan values education as an important tool in music making. He has previously taught at the Eastman School of Music and The Juilliard School and has conducted master classes and lessons in the United States, the Caribbean, South America, and Europe.

snippet.description:
Cliburn Backstage with Greg Anderson (‪     @gregandersonpiano       )

Seventeenth Van Cliburn International Piano Competition
May 21–June 7, 2025

Kotaro Shigemori, Japan, 25
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/kotaro-shigemori

About Kotaro
Kotaro Shigemori began piano lessons with his mother when he was 6, and his passion and talent for the instrument grew quickly. He earned a bachelor’s and artist diploma from Toho Gakuen College in Tokyo under Michiko Okamoto and Katsurako Mikami, and won many national competition prizes in Japan. He says that placing at the Long-Thibaud International Competition in 2022 gave him great motivation and strength; it was at that moment that he could see himself as “a pianist who could be active in the world.” 

Kotaro then moved to France in 2023 to study with Rena Shereshevskaya at the École normale de musique de Paris, Alfred Cortot. Over the last two years, he’s published six columns in Piano Magazine (Japan) about his experiences studying abroad. In addition to appearances at the La Folle Journée, Miyazaki International Music Festival, Ishikawa, and Wind and Green Music Festival, he’s performed at Suntory Hall with the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra, Ishikawa Prefectural Concert Hall with the Orchestra Ensemble Kanazawa, Fukui Concert Hall with Aichi Central Symphony Orchestra, and Paris’ Théâtre du Châtelet with Orchestre de la Garde républicaine. Through performance, he believes musicians “should cherish the feeling of healing the hearts of the listeners.” He was awarded the Ezaki Scholarship in 2023, and the Rohm Music Foundation and Ezoe Memorial Recruit Scholarships in 2024 and 2025.

snippet.description:
Cliburn Backstage with Greg Anderson (‪    @gregandersonpiano     )

Seventeenth Van Cliburn International Piano Competition

Carter Johnson, Canada/United States, 28
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/carter-johnson

About Carter
Carter Johnson only ever remembers wanting to become a concert pianist since his grandmother encouraged him toward the instrument when he was 5. Growing up on Vancouver Island, he studied with Shelley Roberts for 12 years before attending the University of British Columbia, where he completed a bachelor’s under Mark Anderson. He moved to the United States in 2019 to study with Joseph Kalichstein and Matti Raekallio at The Juilliard School (master’s) and has spent the last four years in New Haven, living with his wife and two children while attending the Yale School of Music under the tutelage of Wei-Yi Yang (master’s and now doctorate studies).  

The silver medalist of the 2024 Gina Bachauer International Piano Competition, he has performed with the Montréal Symphony Orchestra, Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra, Orchestre Métropolitain, Utah Symphony, Poznań Philharmonic Orchestra, Victoria Symphony Orchestra, and Orchestra of the Americas, and his playing has been broadcasted by CBC Radio and medici.tv. Venue highlights include the Maison Symphonique, Chan Centre for the Performing Arts, Kaufmann Concert Hall at the 92nd Street Y, Shenzhen Concert Hall, Salle Bourgie, and Warsaw National Philharmonic Hall. 

Carter has a particular interest in bringing light to lesser-explored parts of the repertory, most recently championing a collection of works by nearly forgotten Polish composers. He’s an experienced vocal coach, is enthusiastic about languages, and has also studied oboe, voice, and harpsichord. Trained in elocution as a teenager, he holds an ATCL with distinction in speech and drama from Trinity College London, which serves him well in recital: he loves speaking with audiences to bring them further into the music and its story. He also finds great inspiration outside of classical music—in his family, film, nature, food, and non-classical artists like Björk and Brian Eno, whom he says help him to think outside the box.

Vitaly Starikov, Israel/Russia, 30
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/vitaly-starikov

About Vitaly
Born into a family of musicians, Vitaly Starikov’s journey started when his parents enrolled him to sing in a children’s music group at age 3, and he went on to Ural Musical School for Gifted Children in his native Yekaterinburg at 7. He made his concerto debut at age 10 with the Ural State Russian Folk Orchestra, and his recital debut three years later, in the small hall of the Ural Special Music School. It was at 14 that he committed his life to music. His “dream came true” when he began studying with Vera Gornostayeva, one of the world’s most venerated teachers, at the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory. At that time, her student, Vadym Kholodenko, had just won the 2013 Cliburn Competition, which greatly inspired Vitaly: “and it was then that the thought was born to someday participate in this competition.” He went on to earn his bachelor’s degree at the Conservatory and then his master’s degree, under the tutelage of Eliso Virsaladze. He’s now at the Yale School of Music, pursuing an artist diploma under Boris Berman and is a laureate of the Queen Elisabeth and Sydney International Competitions.

Recital and chamber music appearances have taken him around the world, notably to Austria, Australia, Slovakia, Israel, Cyprus, Italy, France, Belgium, and Malaysia, with highlights including Sydney Opera House, Queen Elisabeth Hall, and the Great Hall of the Moscow Conservatory. He has performed with the Antwerp and Belgian National Orchestras, Sydney Symphony Orchestra, Belarusian State Symphony Orchestra, and St. Petersburg Symphony, and toured with the Orchestre national de Metz Grand Est. He holds a strong commitment to new music and has won accolades for his performances of it, including at the Queen Elisabeth (Belgium), Jaen (Spain), and Taneyev (Russia) international competitions. “I want to present works that reflect not only tradition but also contemporary life, offering new perspectives on familiar music and introducing lesser-known pieces to wider audiences.”

Philipp Lynov, Russia, 26
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/philipp-lynov

About Philipp
Philipp Lynov saw a piano for the first time when he was in kindergarten. The moment left such a lasting impression on him that he credits it—the fascination of owning a piano and childhood curiosity—with his start in music. He started learning at the age of 6 as “simply a source of joy,” then earned a spot at the Central Music School at the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory at the age of 14, studying with Natalia Bogdanova. He went on to complete his bachelor’s there as well, under Eliso Virsaladze. He then moved to Germany, where he's studied with Claudio Martinez Mehner and Nina Tichman at the Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln since 2022.  

Philipp has won first prizes at international competitions, including Xiamen (China), Takamatsu (Japan), and Paderewski (Poland), among others. Concerts have taken him around the globe—to Russia, Germany, Austria, Poland, Spain, Italy, Israel, Switzerland, Australia, and Japan—with highlights including his 2023 debut in the Main Auditorium of the Berlin Philharmonic with the Sinfonieorchester Berlin. When it comes to engaging audiences, he says: “I believe that every person possesses their own unique brilliance. To captivate audiences with music, it’s essential to communicate something meaningful—something that, while not always easy to define, resonates deeply.”

Evren Ozel, United States, 36
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/evren-ozel

About Evren
Evren Ozel’s start in piano was very simple: at the age of 3, he was asked if he wanted to take lessons, and he said yes. Right away, these lessons were his favorite part of the week. “If I got in trouble with my mom, the threat that would set me straight was the threat of taking me out of piano lessons.” After his first international piano competition when he was 14, he was inspired to pursue music professionally. “The colleagues I met who shared an interest in playing music, and the immense repertoire that I learned about over those two weeks helped me understand what an incredibly deep and enriching world that pianists live in.” He’s attended the New England Conservatory of Music in Boston since 2017, studying with Wha Kyung Byun and earning his bachelor’s, master’s, and artist diploma; he is now part of the NEC Institute for Concert Artists. 

Evren is the recipient of 2023 Avery Fisher and 2022 Salon de Virtuosi Career Grants, and a laureate of the Cleveland, Dublin, and Cooper International Piano Competitions. He has been represented by Concert Artists Guild since 2021 as a winner of their Victor Elmaleh Competition. Since his debut with the Minnesota Orchestra at age 11, he has been a featured soloist with the Cleveland Orchestra, Jacksonville Symphony, and Boston Pops Orchestra. He’s performed recitals at La Jolla Music Society, Capital Region Classical, Cal Performances, Schubert Club, Chopin Society of Minnesota, and The Gilmore. His first album of Mozart Concertos with the ORF Radio Symphony of Vienna and conductor Howard Griffiths will be released this year on Alpha Classics. An active chamber musician, he performs alongside artists including Stella Chen, Zlatomir Fung, Paul Huang, and Kim Kashkashian. He spent four summers at the Marlboro Festival and is currently a 2024–2027 Bowers Program Artist for the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center.

Angel Stanislav Wang, United States, 22
https://cliburn.org/competitions/2025-cliburn-competition/2025-competitors/angel-stanislav-wang

About Angel
Angel Stanislav Wang was born into a family of musicians in Los Angeles. His pianist parents are U.S. immigrants—his father originally from China, his mother from Russia—who established a music school in their longtime home in California. Angel was always extremely fond of performing on stage, whether playing the piano, dancing, or singing. As a small child, he would put on shows in their living room, paying careful attention to each detail, from lighting and special effects to costumes and sets. “Classical music was always present. When I first heard the works of Rachmaninov and Tchaikovsky, I ran to the piano, trying to repeat the beautiful harmonic shifts and endless melodies that captivated me when listening to these composers.” His mother began serious piano lessons with him when he was 5, and he immediately showed immense promise. Wanting him to be trained in the same school of music that she had, his mother moved him to her native Moscow in 2013, where he would live with his grandparents and attend the Gnessin Special School of Music (with Tatiana Zelikman). He joined Natalia Trull’s studio at Central Music School and then the Moscow Tchaikovsky Conservatory in 2020, where he continues to study today. 

A winner of more than 35 international competitions (and a silver medal at the 2023 Tchaikovsky), Angel regularly concertizes in the United States, Germany, Russia, Switzerland, Austria, Spain, Italy, Croatia; he’s performed at Carnegie Hall, Musikverein (Vienna, Austria), the Great, Small, and Rachmaninov Halls of the Moscow Conservatory, Concert Halls of the Mariinsky Theatre (St. Petersburg), and Tchaikovsky Concert Hall (Moscow). The 22-year-old loves traveling to different countries: “Whenever I have the chance, I visit different museums, theatres, and art exhibitions. It is interesting to experience the different cultures, mentalities, and ideas, as well as interests, of other people.”

snippet.title: "The Brothers Concerto" by Leonardo and Peter Dugan Teaser
snippet.description:
The Brothers Concerto revisits life moments that encapsulate the unique experience of siblinghood: Tales of make-believe monsters. An anxious car ride. A little brother glad to tag along with his big brother, unknowingly developing the foundation of their closeness and mutual respect in adulthood. Unfaltering support through life’s greatest challenges.

Leonardo and Peter Dugan grew up in Philadelphia, where their musical development was steeped in both the jazz and classical traditions. The language of the Concerto reflects the commonality and individuality of brothers, of two musical idioms, of an orchestra and its soloist. Soaring, lyrical melodies, propulsive rhythms, and Leonardo’s characteristic lush orchestration frame the athletic virtuosity of Peter’s pianism. It’s an inspired combination—classical structure and counterpoint with improvised solos using the vocabulary of jazz.

pl.title: „Koncert Braci” Leonarda i Petera Dugana – zwiastun
pl.description:
Koncert Braci przywołuje chwile z życia, które oddają wyjątkowe doświadczenie rodzeństwa: opowieści o wyimaginowanych potworach. Niespokojna podróż samochodem. Młodszy brat, który z radością towarzyszy starszemu bratu, nieświadomie budując fundamenty ich bliskości i wzajemnego szacunku w dorosłym życiu. Niezachwiane wsparcie w obliczu największych wyzwań życiowych.

Leonardo i Peter Dugan dorastali w Filadelfii, gdzie ich rozwój muzyczny był przesiąknięty zarówno tradycją jazzową, jak i klasyczną. Język Koncertu odzwierciedla wspólnotę i indywidualność braci, dwóch muzycznych idiomów, orkiestry i jej solisty. Wznoszące się, liryczne melodie, porywające rytmy i charakterystyczna dla Leonarda bogata orkiestracja tworzą ramy dla atletycznej wirtuozerii pianistycznej Petera. To inspirujące połączenie – klasycznej struktury i kontrapunktu z improwizowanymi solówkami, wykorzystującymi słownictwo jazzowe.

nl-NL.title: "The Brothers Concerto" van Leonardo en Peter Dugan - Teaser
nl-NL.description:
Het Brothers Concerto blikt terug op momenten uit het leven die de unieke ervaring van broederschap treffend weergeven: verhalen over verzonnen monsters, een angstige autorit, een jongere broer die graag met zijn oudere broer meereist en zo onbewust de basis legt voor hun hechte band en wederzijds respect in hun volwassen leven, en onvoorwaardelijke steun in de grootste uitdagingen van het leven.

Leonardo en Peter Dugan groeiden op in Philadelphia, waar hun muzikale ontwikkeling doordrenkt was van zowel de jazz- als de klassieke traditie. De taal van het Concerto weerspiegelt de overeenkomsten en verschillen tussen broers, tussen twee muzikale idiomen, tussen een orkest en zijn solist. Meeslepende, lyrische melodieën, stuwend ritme en Leonardo's kenmerkende weelderige orkestratie omlijsten de atletische virtuositeit van Peters pianospel. Het is een geïnspireerde combinatie: klassieke structuur en contrapunt met geïmproviseerde solo's die gebruikmaken van de jazzvocabulaire.

ta.title: லியோனார்டோ மற்றும் பீட்டர் டுகன் எழுதிய "தி பிரதர்ஸ் கான்செர்டோ" டீசர்
ta.description:
சகோதரத்துவத்தின் தனித்துவமான அனுபவத்தை உள்ளடக்கிய வாழ்க்கை தருணங்களை பிரதர்ஸ் கான்செர்டோ மீண்டும் நினைவுபடுத்துகிறது: கற்பனையான அரக்கர்களின் கதைகள். ஒரு பதட்டமான கார் சவாரி. தனது பெரிய சகோதரனுடன் சேர்ந்து மகிழ்ச்சியாக இருக்கும் ஒரு சிறிய சகோதரர், அறியாமலேயே அவர்களின் நெருக்கம் மற்றும் பரஸ்பர மரியாதையின் அடித்தளத்தை வளர்த்துக் கொள்கிறார். வாழ்க்கையின் மிகப்பெரிய சவால்களின் மூலம் தடுமாறாத ஆதரவு.

லியோனார்டோ மற்றும் பீட்டர் டூகன் பிலடெல்பியாவில் வளர்ந்தனர், அங்கு அவர்களின் இசை வளர்ச்சி ஜாஸ் மற்றும் கிளாசிக்கல் மரபுகள் இரண்டிலும் ஊறிப்போனது. கான்செர்டோவின் மொழி சகோதரர்களின் பொதுவான தன்மை மற்றும் தனித்துவத்தை பிரதிபலிக்கிறது, இரண்டு இசை மரபுகள், ஒரு இசைக்குழு மற்றும் அதன் தனிப்பாடகர். உயரும், பாடல் வரிகள் கொண்ட மெல்லிசைகள், உந்துவிசை தாளங்கள் மற்றும் லியோனார்டோவின் சிறப்பியல்பு நிறைந்த இசைக்குழு பீட்டரின் பியானிசத்தின் தடகள திறமையை வடிவமைக்கிறது. இது ஒரு ஈர்க்கப்பட்ட கலவையாகும் - ஜாஸின் சொற்களஞ்சியத்தைப் பயன்படுத்தி மேம்படுத்தப்பட்ட தனிப்பாடல்களுடன் கிளாசிக்கல் அமைப்பு மற்றும் எதிர்முனை.

hi.title: लियोनार्डो और पीटर डुगन द्वारा रचित "द ब्रदर्स कॉन्सर्टो" का टीज़र
hi.description:
ब्रदर्स कॉन्सर्टो भाई-बहन के अनूठे अनुभव को समेटे हुए जीवन के उन पलों को फिर से जीवंत करता है: काल्पनिक राक्षसों की कहानियाँ। एक चिंताजनक कार यात्रा। एक छोटा भाई अपने बड़े भाई के साथ खुशी-खुशी सफर करता है, अनजाने में ही उनके बीच घनिष्ठता और वयस्कता में आपसी सम्मान की नींव रखता है। जीवन की सबसे बड़ी चुनौतियों में अटूट समर्थन।

लियोनार्डो और पीटर डुगन फिलाडेल्फिया में पले-बढ़े, जहाँ उनका संगीत विकास जैज़ और शास्त्रीय दोनों परंपराओं से ओतप्रोत था। कॉन्सर्टो की भाषा भाइयों की समानता और विशिष्टता, दो संगीत शैलियों, एक ऑर्केस्ट्रा और उसके एकल वादक की समानता और विशिष्टता को दर्शाती है। ऊँची, गीतात्मक धुनें, प्रेरक लय और लियोनार्डो की विशिष्ट भव्य ऑर्केस्ट्रेशन पीटर के पियानो वादन की निपुणता को निखारती हैं। यह एक प्रेरणादायक संयोजन है—शास्त्रीय संरचना और काउंटरपॉइंट के साथ जैज़ की शब्दावली का उपयोग करते हुए तात्कालिक एकल वादन।

es-US.title: "El concierto de los hermanos" de Leonardo y Peter Dugan - Avance
es-US.description:
El Concierto para Hermanos retoma momentos de la vida que encapsulan la experiencia única de la hermandad: Historias de monstruos imaginarios. Un viaje en coche lleno de ansiedad. Un hermano pequeño feliz de acompañar a su hermano mayor, construyendo sin saberlo las bases de su cercanía y respeto mutuo en la edad adulta. Un apoyo incondicional ante los mayores desafíos de la vida.

Leonardo y Peter Dugan crecieron en Filadelfia, donde su desarrollo musical estuvo impregnado tanto del jazz como de la tradición clásica. El lenguaje del Concierto refleja las similitudes e individualidades de los hermanos, de dos lenguajes musicales, de una orquesta y su solista. Melodías líricas y evocadoras, ritmos impulsivos y la exuberante orquestación característica de Leonardo enmarcan el virtuosismo atlético del pianismo de Peter. Es una combinación inspirada: estructura clásica y contrapunto con solos improvisados ​​que utilizan el vocabulario del jazz.

bn.title: লিওনার্দো এবং পিটার ডুগানের "দ্য ব্রাদার্স কনসার্টো" টিজার
bn.description:
ব্রাদার্স কনসার্টো জীবনের সেই মুহূর্তগুলিকে পুনর্বিবেচনা করে যা ভাইবোনের অনন্য অভিজ্ঞতাকে ধারণ করে: কাল্পনিক দানবের গল্প। একটি উদ্বিগ্ন গাড়ি ভ্রমণ। একটি ছোট ভাই তার বড় ভাইয়ের সাথে একসাথে থাকতে পেরে আনন্দিত, অজান্তেই প্রাপ্তবয়স্ক অবস্থায় তাদের ঘনিষ্ঠতা এবং পারস্পরিক শ্রদ্ধার ভিত্তি গড়ে তোলে। জীবনের সবচেয়ে বড় চ্যালেঞ্জগুলির মধ্যে অবিচল সমর্থন।

লিওনার্দো এবং পিটার ডুগান ফিলাডেলফিয়ায় বেড়ে ওঠেন, যেখানে তাদের সঙ্গীত বিকাশ জ্যাজ এবং ধ্রুপদী উভয় ঐতিহ্যের মধ্যেই নিহিত ছিল। কনসার্টোর ভাষা ভাইদের মধ্যে, দুটি সঙ্গীতের বাগধারার, একটি অর্কেস্ট্রা এবং এর একক বাদকের সাধারণতা এবং ব্যক্তিত্বকে প্রতিফলিত করে। উড্ডয়নশীল, গীতিমূলক সুর, প্ররোচনামূলক ছন্দ এবং লিওনার্দোর বৈশিষ্ট্যপূর্ণ মনোরম অর্কেস্ট্রেশন পিটারের পিয়ানোবাদের অ্যাথলেটিক ভার্চুওসিটিকে ফ্রেম করে। এটি একটি অনুপ্রাণিত সমন্বয় - জ্যাজের শব্দভাণ্ডার ব্যবহার করে উন্নত এককের সাথে ধ্রুপদী কাঠামো এবং প্রতিবিম্ব।

iw.title: טיזר ל"קונצ'רטו האחים" מאת לאונרדו ופיטר דוגן
iw.description:
הקונצ'רטו של האחים מבקר מחדש רגעים בחיים אשר מסכמים את החוויה הייחודית של אחאות: סיפורים על מפלצות דמיוניות. נסיעה חרדתית במכונית. אח קטן ששמח להצטרף לאחיו הגדול, ומפתח מבלי דעת את היסודות לקרבה ולכבוד ההדדי ביניהם בבגרות. תמיכה בלתי מתפשרת באתגרים הגדולים ביותר של החיים.

לאונרדו ופיטר דוגן גדלו בפילדלפיה, שם התפתחותם המוזיקלית הייתה שקועה הן במסורת הג'אז והן במסורת הקלאסית. שפת הקונצ'רטו משקפת את המשותף והאינדיבידואליות של האחים, של שני ניבים מוזיקליים, של תזמורת וסולנית. מנגינות ליריות עזות, מקצבים מניעים והתזמור השופע האופייני של לאונרדו ממסגרים את הווירטואוזיות האתלטית של הפסנתרנות של פיטר. זהו שילוב מעורר השראה - מבנה קלאסי וקונטרהפונקט עם סולואים מאולתרים המשתמשים באוצר המילים של הג'אז.

ko.title: 레오나르도와 피터 듀건의 "형제 협주곡" 티저
ko.description:
형제 협주곡은 형제간의 특별한 경험을 담은 삶의 순간들을 되짚어봅니다. 상상 속 괴물 이야기, 불안한 차 안에서의 시간, 형을 따라다니는 동생의 모습, 그 순간들이 어른이 되어서도 변치 않는 형제애와 상호 존중의 토대가 됩니다. 인생의 가장 큰 시련 속에서도 변함없는 지지를 주고받는 모습까지.

레오나르도와 피터 두간 형제는 필라델피아에서 자라면서 재즈와 클래식 음악의 영향을 깊이 받았습니다. 이 협주곡은 형제의 공통점과 개성, 두 가지 음악적 어법, 오케스트라와 독주자의 조화를 음악으로 표현합니다. 솟아오르는 듯한 서정적인 멜로디, 역동적인 리듬, 그리고 레오나르도 특유의 풍성한 오케스트레이션은 피터의 역동적인 피아노 기교를 더욱 돋보이게 합니다. 클래식 음악의 구조와 대위법에 재즈의 어휘를 활용한 즉흥 독주가 어우러진 이 작품은 영감을 주는 조합입니다.

ja.title: レオナルドとピーター・デュガンによる「兄弟協奏曲」ティーザー
ja.description:
兄弟協奏曲は、兄弟ならではの特別な経験を凝縮した人生の瞬間を彷彿とさせます。空想上の怪物たちの物語。不安な車内での出来事。兄に付いていくことを喜ぶ弟。知らず知らずのうちに、大人になってからの親密さと相互尊重の基盤を育んでいく弟。人生最大の試練を乗り越える揺るぎない支え。

レオナルドとピーター・デュガンはフィラデルフィアで育ち、ジャズとクラシック音楽の伝統に深く根ざした音楽性を築きました。協奏曲の言語は、兄弟、二つの音楽表現、オーケストラとソリストという、共通性と個性を反映しています。高揚感あふれる叙情的なメロディー、力強いリズム、そしてレオナルド特有の豊かなオーケストレーションが、ピーターのピアニズムの卓越した技巧を際立たせています。クラシック音楽の構造と対位法、そしてジャズの語彙を用いた即興ソロが織りなす、まさに刺激的な融合です。

id.title: Cuplikan "The Brothers Concerto" karya Leonardo dan Peter Dugan
id.description:
Konserto Saudara ini mengulas kembali momen-momen kehidupan yang merangkum pengalaman unik persaudaraan: Kisah-kisah tentang monster khayalan. Perjalanan mobil yang menegangkan. Seorang adik laki-laki yang senang ikut bersama kakak laki-lakinya, tanpa disadari mengembangkan fondasi kedekatan dan rasa saling menghormati mereka di masa dewasa. Dukungan yang tak tergoyahkan melalui tantangan terbesar dalam hidup.

Leonardo dan Peter Dugan tumbuh di Philadelphia, di mana perkembangan musik mereka dipengaruhi oleh tradisi jazz dan klasik. Bahasa Konserto ini mencerminkan kesamaan dan individualitas saudara, dua idiom musik, sebuah orkestra dan soloisnya. Melodi yang melambung dan liris, ritme yang menggerakkan, dan orkestrasi Leonardo yang kaya membingkai virtuosisme atletis pianisme Peter. Ini adalah kombinasi yang menginspirasi—struktur dan kontrapung klasik dengan solo improvisasi menggunakan kosakata jazz.

ml.title: ലിയോനാർഡോയും പീറ്റർ ഡുഗനും ചേർന്ന് "ദി ബ്രദേഴ്‌സ് കൺസേർട്ടോ" എന്ന ഗാനത്തിന്റെ ടീസർ
ml.description:
സഹോദര ബന്ധത്തിന്റെ അതുല്യമായ അനുഭവത്തെ ഉൾക്കൊള്ളുന്ന ജീവിത നിമിഷങ്ങളെ ബ്രദേഴ്‌സ് കൺസേർട്ടോ വീണ്ടും അവതരിപ്പിക്കുന്നു: സാങ്കൽപ്പിക രാക്ഷസന്മാരുടെ കഥകൾ. ഉത്കണ്ഠാകുലമായ ഒരു കാർ യാത്ര. തന്റെ മൂത്ത സഹോദരനോടൊപ്പം ചേരാൻ സന്തോഷിക്കുന്ന ഒരു ചെറിയ സഹോദരൻ, പ്രായപൂർത്തിയായപ്പോൾ അറിയാതെ അവരുടെ അടുപ്പത്തിന്റെയും പരസ്പര ബഹുമാനത്തിന്റെയും അടിത്തറ വികസിപ്പിക്കുന്നു. ജീവിതത്തിലെ ഏറ്റവും വലിയ വെല്ലുവിളികളിലൂടെ അചഞ്ചലമായ പിന്തുണ.

ലിയോനാർഡോയും പീറ്റർ ഡുഗനും ഫിലാഡൽഫിയയിലാണ് വളർന്നത്, അവിടെ അവരുടെ സംഗീത വികസനം ജാസ്, ക്ലാസിക്കൽ പാരമ്പര്യങ്ങളിൽ മുങ്ങിക്കുളിച്ചു. കൺസേർട്ടോയുടെ ഭാഷ സഹോദരങ്ങളുടെ, രണ്ട് സംഗീത ഭാഷാഭേദങ്ങളുടെ, ഒരു ഓർക്കസ്ട്രയുടെയും അതിന്റെ സോളോയിസ്റ്റിന്റെയും പൊതുവായ വ്യക്തിത്വത്തെയും വ്യക്തിത്വത്തെയും പ്രതിഫലിപ്പിക്കുന്നു. കുതിച്ചുയരുന്ന, ഗാനരചനാ മെലഡികൾ, പ്രോപ്പൽസീവ് താളങ്ങൾ, ലിയോനാർഡോയുടെ സ്വഭാവസവിശേഷതയായ സമൃദ്ധമായ ഓർക്കസ്ട്രേഷൻ എന്നിവ പീറ്ററിന്റെ പിയാനിസത്തിന്റെ കായിക വൈദഗ്ധ്യത്തെ രൂപപ്പെടുത്തുന്നു. ഇത് ഒരു പ്രചോദനാത്മക സംയോജനമാണ് - ജാസിന്റെ പദാവലി ഉപയോഗിച്ച് ഇംപ്രൊവൈസ്ഡ് സോളോകളുള്ള ക്ലാസിക്കൽ ഘടനയും പ്രതിബിംബവും.

pt-BR.title: "O Concerto dos Irmãos" de Leonardo e Peter Dugan (Apresentação)
pt-BR.description:
O Concerto dos Irmãos revisita momentos da vida que encapsulam a experiência única da irmandade: histórias de monstros imaginários; uma viagem de carro angustiante; um irmão mais novo feliz por acompanhar o mais velho, construindo, sem saber, a base da proximidade e do respeito mútuo que os acompanharia na vida adulta; apoio inabalável nos maiores desafios da vida.

Leonardo e Peter Dugan cresceram na Filadélfia, onde seu desenvolvimento musical foi imerso tanto na tradição do jazz quanto na música clássica. A linguagem do Concerto reflete a comunhão e a individualidade dos irmãos, de duas linguagens musicais, de uma orquestra e seu solista. Melodias líricas e arrebatadoras, ritmos pulsantes e a orquestração exuberante característica de Leonardo emolduram o virtuosismo atlético do pianismo de Peter. É uma combinação inspirada: estrutura clássica e contraponto com solos improvisados ​​utilizando a linguagem do jazz.

en.title: "The Brothers Concerto" by Leonardo and Peter Dugan Teaser
en.description:
The Brothers Concerto revisits life moments that encapsulate the unique experience of siblinghood: Tales of make-believe monsters. An anxious car ride. A little brother glad to tag along with his big brother, unknowingly developing the foundation of their closeness and mutual respect in adulthood. Unfaltering support through life’s greatest challenges.

Leonardo and Peter Dugan grew up in Philadelphia, where their musical development was steeped in both the jazz and classical traditions. The language of the Concerto reflects the commonality and individuality of brothers, of two musical idioms, of an orchestra and its soloist. Soaring, lyrical melodies, propulsive rhythms, and Leonardo’s characteristic lush orchestration frame the athletic virtuosity of Peter’s pianism. It’s an inspired combination—classical structure and counterpoint with improvised solos using the vocabulary of jazz.

fr-FR.title: Extrait du « Concerto des frères » de Leonardo et Peter Dugan
fr-FR.description:
Le Concerto des Frères revisite des moments de vie qui incarnent l'expérience unique de la fraternité : des histoires de monstres imaginaires, un trajet en voiture angoissant, un petit frère heureux d'accompagner son grand frère, jetant sans le savoir les bases de leur complicité et de leur respect mutuel à l'âge adulte, un soutien indéfectible face aux plus grandes épreuves de la vie.

Leonardo et Peter Dugan ont grandi à Philadelphie, où leur formation musicale s'est imprégnée des traditions jazz et classique. Le langage du Concerto reflète la dualité et la singularité des frères, de deux idiomes musicaux, d'un orchestre et de son soliste. Des mélodies lyriques et aériennes, des rythmes entraînants et l'orchestration luxuriante caractéristique de Leonardo mettent en valeur la virtuosité athlétique du jeu pianistique de Peter. C'est une combinaison inspirée : une structure et un contrepoint classiques alliés à des solos improvisés puisant dans le vocabulaire du jazz.

uk.title: «Концерт братів» Леонардо та Пітера Дугана, тизер
uk.description:
Концерт «Брати» переживає життєві моменти, що втілюють унікальний досвід братства та сестринства: історії про вигаданих монстрів. Тривожна поїздка на машині. Молодший брат, який радий приєднатися до свого старшого брата, несвідомо розвиваючи основу їхньої близькості та взаємної поваги в дорослому віці. Непохитну підтримку під час найбільших життєвих випробувань.

Леонардо та Пітер Дуган виросли у Філадельфії, де їхній музичний розвиток був просякнутий як джазовими, так і класичними традиціями. Мова Концерту відображає спільність та індивідуальність братів, двох музичних ідіом, оркестру та його соліста. Злітні, ліричні мелодії, імпульсивні ритми та характерна пишна оркестровка Леонардо обрамляють атлетичну віртуозність піанізму Пітера. Це натхненне поєднання — класична структура та контрапункт з імпровізованими соло з використанням джазової лексики.

de-DE.title: „Das Brüderkonzert“ von Leonardo und Peter Dugan (Teaser)
de-DE.description:
Das Brüderkonzert lässt Momente des Lebens wiederaufleben, die die einzigartige Erfahrung der Geschwisterliebe einfangen: Geschichten von Fantasiemonstern. Eine aufregende Autofahrt. Ein kleiner Bruder, der freudig seinen großen Bruder begleitet und dabei unbewusst den Grundstein für ihre enge Verbundenheit und ihren gegenseitigen Respekt im Erwachsenenalter legt. Unerschütterliche Unterstützung in den größten Herausforderungen des Lebens.

Leonardo und Peter Dugan wuchsen in Philadelphia auf, wo ihre musikalische Entwicklung sowohl von der Jazz- als auch von der klassischen Tradition geprägt war. Die Tonsprache des Konzerts spiegelt die Gemeinsamkeiten und die Individualität der Brüder, zweier musikalischer Idiome, eines Orchesters und seines Solisten wider. Erhabene, lyrische Melodien, mitreißende Rhythmen und Leonardos charakteristisch üppige Orchestrierung umrahmen die virtuose Virtuosität von Peters Klavierspiel. Es ist eine inspirierte Kombination – klassische Struktur und Kontrapunkt mit improvisierten Soli im Vokabular des Jazz.

pa.title: ਲਿਓਨਾਰਡੋ ਅਤੇ ਪੀਟਰ ਡੂਗਨ ਦੁਆਰਾ "ਦਿ ਬ੍ਰਦਰਜ਼ ਕੰਸਰਟੋ" ਦਾ ਟੀਜ਼ਰ
pa.description:
ਬ੍ਰਦਰਜ਼ ਕੰਸਰਟੋ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਦੇ ਪਲਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਦੁਬਾਰਾ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਭੈਣ-ਭਰਾ ਦੇ ਵਿਲੱਖਣ ਅਨੁਭਵ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੇਟਦੇ ਹਨ: ਨਕਲੀ ਰਾਖਸ਼ਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਹਾਣੀਆਂ। ਇੱਕ ਬੇਚੈਨ ਕਾਰ ਸਵਾਰੀ। ਇੱਕ ਛੋਟਾ ਭਰਾ ਆਪਣੇ ਵੱਡੇ ਭਰਾ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਨ ਲਈ ਖੁਸ਼ ਹੈ, ਅਣਜਾਣੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਾਲਗਤਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਨੇੜਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਸੀ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਦੀ ਨੀਂਹ ਵਿਕਸਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਚੁਣੌਤੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਲੰਘਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਡੋਲ ਸਮਰਥਨ।

ਲਿਓਨਾਰਡੋ ਅਤੇ ਪੀਟਰ ਡੂਗਨ ਫਿਲਾਡੇਲਫੀਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਡੇ ਹੋਏ, ਜਿੱਥੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਸੰਗੀਤਕ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਜੈਜ਼ ਅਤੇ ਕਲਾਸੀਕਲ ਪਰੰਪਰਾਵਾਂ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਡੁੱਬਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੀ। ਕੰਸਰਟੋ ਦੀ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਭਰਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਾਂਝੀਵਾਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਅਕਤੀਗਤਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਦਰਸਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ, ਦੋ ਸੰਗੀਤਕ ਮੁਹਾਵਰਿਆਂ ਦੀ, ਇੱਕ ਆਰਕੈਸਟਰਾ ਅਤੇ ਇਸਦੇ ਸੋਲੋਇਸਟ ਦੀ। ਉੱਡਦੇ, ਗੀਤਕਾਰੀ ਧੁਨਾਂ, ਪ੍ਰੇਰਕ ਤਾਲਾਂ, ਅਤੇ ਲਿਓਨਾਰਡੋ ਦੀ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਤਾ ਭਰਪੂਰ ਆਰਕੈਸਟ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਪੀਟਰ ਦੇ ਪਿਆਨੋਵਾਦ ਦੀ ਐਥਲੈਟਿਕ ਗੁਣ ਨੂੰ ਫਰੇਮ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਿਤ ਸੁਮੇਲ ਹੈ - ਜੈਜ਼ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਵਲੀ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਦੇ ਹੋਏ ਸੁਧਾਰੇ ਗਏ ਸੋਲੋ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਕਲਾਸੀਕਲ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਰੋਧੀ ਬਿੰਦੂ।

te.title: లియోనార్డో మరియు పీటర్ డ్యూగన్ రాసిన "ది బ్రదర్స్ కాన్సర్టో" టీజర్
te.description:
ది బ్రదర్స్ కాన్సెర్టో జీవిత క్షణాలను తిరిగి గుర్తుకు తెస్తుంది, అవి తోబుట్టువుల అనుబంధం యొక్క ప్రత్యేకమైన అనుభవాన్ని సంగ్రహిస్తాయి: నకిలీ రాక్షసుల కథలు. ఆత్రుతతో కూడిన కారు ప్రయాణం. తన పెద్ద తమ్ముడితో కలిసి ఉండటానికి సంతోషంగా ఉన్న ఒక చిన్న సోదరుడు, తెలియకుండానే వారి సాన్నిహిత్యం మరియు పరస్పర గౌరవం యొక్క పునాదిని యుక్తవయస్సులో అభివృద్ధి చేస్తాడు. జీవితంలోని అతిపెద్ద సవాళ్ల ద్వారా తడబడని మద్దతు.

లియోనార్డో మరియు పీటర్ డ్యూగన్ ఫిలడెల్ఫియాలో పెరిగారు, అక్కడ వారి సంగీత అభివృద్ధి జాజ్ మరియు శాస్త్రీయ సంప్రదాయాలలో మునిగిపోయింది. కాన్సెర్టో భాష సోదరుల యొక్క సాధారణత మరియు వ్యక్తిత్వాన్ని ప్రతిబింబిస్తుంది, రెండు సంగీత ఇడియమ్‌లు, ఆర్కెస్ట్రా మరియు దాని సోలో వాద్యకారుడు. ఎగురుతున్న, లిరికల్ మెలోడీలు, ప్రొపల్సివ్ లయలు మరియు లియోనార్డో యొక్క లక్షణమైన లష్ ఆర్కెస్ట్రేషన్ పీటర్ పియానిజం యొక్క అథ్లెటిక్ నైపుణ్యాన్ని రూపొందిస్తాయి. ఇది ప్రేరేపిత కలయిక - జాజ్ పదజాలాన్ని ఉపయోగించి ఇంప్రూవైజ్డ్ సోలోలతో క్లాసికల్ నిర్మాణం మరియు కౌంటర్ పాయింట్.

ar.title: "كونشيرتو الإخوة" من تأليف ليوناردو وبيتر دوجان - مقطع دعائي
ar.description:
تستحضر كونشيرتو الإخوة لحظاتٍ من الحياة تُجسّد تجربة الأخوة الفريدة: حكايات عن وحوشٍ خيالية، رحلةٌ مُقلقة بالسيارة، أخٌ صغيرٌ سعيدٌ بمرافقة أخيه الأكبر، يُرسي دون وعيٍ منه أساسَ علاقتهما الوثيقة واحترامهما المتبادل في مرحلة البلوغ، ودعمٌ ثابتٌ في مواجهة أعظم تحديات الحياة.

نشأ ليوناردو وبيتر دوغان في فيلادلفيا، حيث تشبّع نموهما الموسيقي بتقاليد موسيقى الجاز والموسيقى الكلاسيكية. تعكس لغة الكونشيرتو القواسم المشتركة والفردية بين الإخوة، وبين أسلوبين موسيقيين، وبين الأوركسترا وعازفها المنفرد. ألحانٌ عذبةٌ وساحرة، وإيقاعاتٌ دافعة، وتوزيعٌ موسيقيٌّ فخمٌ يُميّز أسلوب ليوناردو، يُؤطّر براعة بيتر في العزف على البيانو. إنه مزيجٌ مُلهم - بنيةٌ كلاسيكيةٌ وتناغمٌ مع عزفٍ منفردٍ مرتجلٍ باستخدام مفردات موسيقى الجاز.

ru.title: Анонс концерта братьев Леонардо и Питера Дуганов.
ru.description:
Концерт для братьев переосмысливает моменты жизни, отражающие уникальный опыт братско-сестринских отношений: истории о вымышленных монстрах, тревожная поездка на машине, младший брат, с радостью сопровождающий старшего, неосознанно закладывающий основу их близости и взаимного уважения во взрослой жизни, непоколебимая поддержка в самых сложных жизненных ситуациях.

Леонардо и Питер Дуган выросли в Филадельфии, где их музыкальное развитие проходило под влиянием как джазовых, так и классических традиций. Язык Концерта отражает общность и индивидуальность братьев, двух музыкальных стилей, оркестра и его солиста. Парящие, лирические мелодии, энергичные ритмы и характерная для Леонардо пышная оркестровка обрамляют виртуозную игру Питера на фортепиано. Это вдохновенное сочетание — классическая структура и контрапункт с импровизированными соло, использующими лексику джаза.

it.title: Teaser di "The Brothers Concerto" di Leonardo e Peter Dugan
it.description:
Il Concerto dei Fratelli rivisita momenti di vita che racchiudono l'esperienza unica della fratellanza: storie di mostri immaginari. Un viaggio in macchina pieno di ansia. Un fratellino felice di seguire il fratello maggiore, sviluppando inconsapevolmente le basi della loro vicinanza e del rispetto reciproco in età adulta. Un sostegno incrollabile nelle più grandi sfide della vita.

Leonardo e Peter Dugan sono cresciuti a Philadelphia, dove il loro sviluppo musicale è stato intriso sia di jazz che di tradizione classica. Il linguaggio del Concerto riflette la comunanza e l'individualità di fratelli, di due idiomi musicali, di un'orchestra e del suo solista. Melodie liriche e slanciate, ritmi propulsivi e la caratteristica lussureggiante orchestrazione di Leonardo incorniciano il virtuosismo atletico del pianismo di Peter. È una combinazione ispirata: struttura classica e contrappunto con assoli improvvisati che utilizzano il vocabolario del jazz.

snippet.title: The Cliburn Agency
snippet.description:
The Cliburn Agency is a full-service boutique firm that offers comprehensive general management, concert booking, project management, and publicity and branding services to a select group of rising and established instrumentalists—piano and beyond—whose high artistic caliber is matched by a vision for moving the field of classical music forward.

The Cliburn Agency roster comprises Anderson & Roe Piano Duo (@andersonroe);  Greg Anderson, piano (@gregandersonpiano) ; Peter Dugan, piano (@peterdugan9983) ; Fei-Fei, piano (@feifeipianist) ; Bridget Kibbey, harp (@bridgetkibbey);  Joshua Roman, cello (@JoshuaRomanCello) ; and Clayton Stephenson, piano (@Claytonplayspiano) . From intriguing programming and projects to alternative concerts and community engagement, the touring musicians of the Agency roster are dedicated to connection and creativity—and they are partnering with the Cliburn to enhance and magnify their careers, efforts, and impact.

Learn more at https://cliburnagency.com/

“The Cliburn Agency is a compelling expansion of the Cliburn’s brand and impact. Our core mission is to support artists and continuously advance classical music. The management and promotion of exceptional musicians—particularly those with a specific fervor and dedication for expanding audiences and breaking down barriers—is the next step in realizing that mission. Through this new program, the Cliburn develops another powerful way to meet the moment and find new ways to expand classical music’s reach as a source of commonality and shared experience in today’s world.”
– Jacques Marquis, president & CEO
